newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks off at midday on renewed rate jitters.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks off at midday on renewed rate jitters.

text.p: Wall Street stocks followed bonds modestly lower at midday losses as last Friday's durable goods report continued to take its toll on frayed investor nerves.

The Dow industrials slipped 26 points to 5696 and the Nasdaq Composite fell four points to 1139. The declines mirrored modest losses in the bond market, where the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury fell 8/32 to yield 6.97 percent.
The losses were evidence of an increasingly unsettled outlook on Wall Street about interest rates, said analysts.
"It's a reaction to the bond market," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "Certainly there's a bit more nervousness about whether interest rates will go up before the election."

Analysts said the fact that one report -- in this case last Friday's strong durable goods figures -- was able to undo a month's worth of stable inflation data was a sign the market was headed for even choppier times.
"This is a rather jittery market if it is willing to change course on just one number," said Michael Metz chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.
"Conviction levels are lower and therefore the market is going to be vulnerable to short-term swings," Metz said.
In the midst of the gloom, tobacco companies showed sudden signs of life after the industry's victory late Friday in an Indiana liability lawsuit.

While the verdict itself was a small victory, it may provide a temporary breather for the beleaguered industry. Philip Morris Cos Inc gained 3-1/4 to 91-1/4 and RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp rose 1-1/8 to 26-5/8.

Telecommunications stocks were also very busy in an otherwise quiet session, after MFS Communications Co Inc and WorldCom Inc agreed to merge creating a fourth giant in the long-distance telephone business.
News of the deal, under which WorldCom will swap 2.1 shares for each MFS share, sent MFS soaring 10 points to 44-7/8. WorldCom shares slid four points to 22-3/8, however.
Analysts said the deal was likely to heighten investor interest in the rest of the sector and telecoms stocks were scattered among the NYSE and Nasdaq most active lists.
"This heats up the merger outlook for other telephone companies," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.

MCI Communications Corp, which early today announced it would buy 10 billion minutes of wireless communications capacity from NextWave Telecom Inc for resale to its own customers, rose 1/8 to 25-5/8 on volume of 2.2 million shares.
AT&T Corp lost one point to 53-5/8 and Sprint Corp eased 1/8 to 39-3/4. Teleport Communications Group Inc surged 2-1/2 to 24-3/4
